messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Finding units from cells
parts:
Hi, How can I find out what unit a particular cell is in? Similarly,
if I know a group name, how can I find out what unit it is in? (my own
attempt to solve the latter needs an answer to the first...)
Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Finding units from cells
parts:
Hi,

you basically have to do this manually.

Cell-to-unit map:
Create a flat unit-to-cell index map as I suggested in a previous
message. The use this to map cell to unit indices.

Group name-to-unit map:
In most cases this is not a bijective map (though it depends on the
CDF). For instance, in SNP chips the group names are "A", "C", "G",
or "T" for all SNP units. I know that for some CDFs they paste the
unit name in front of the group name, but in that case one can easily
infer the unit name from the group name. However^2, the current
affxparser strips out unit names from the group names (mainly to save
memory but also for other reasons which takes to long to explain).
Ken modified affxparser recently to make this optional, but that
version is yet not on BioC. To conclude, I would not try to map group
name to unit(s). Whatever you try to do, could you do it in another
way?

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Finding units from cells
parts:
> However^2, the current
> affxparser strips out unit names from the group names (mainly to save
> memory but also for other reasons which takes to long to explain).
> Ken modified affxparser recently to make this optional, but that
> version is yet not on BioC. To conclude, I would not try to map group
> name to unit(s).

I came up with a little workaround for this, which should do what Elizabeth
wants for exon arrays, at least until affxparser is updated:

groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname);
blanks <- which(unlist(lapply(groupNames, function(x){all(x=="")})));
groupNames[blanks] <- names(groupNames)[blanks];

Cheers,

Ken

messages.subject: Re: Finding units from cells
parts:
I can understand that in general, it isn't always useful to find the
unit name from a group name since they are not always unique, which is
why I was thinking there would be a function that would do it for a
cell index which is unique. I guess you were suggesting, Henrik, that
get *all* cell indices and then flatten them to get a cell->unit
mapping?

> cells <- getCellIndices(cdf)
> flattenCellIndices(cells)

Wouldn't that be terribly slow (to get all of the cells?)

However, Ken's approach satisfies what I need for my exon arrays where
the group names are unique.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

> > flattenCellIndices(cells)

Yes, that would be slow. Ideally affxparser implements this directly
and then it would be fast. A work around is to cache the results to
file, something like (just a sketch - not tested):

setMethodS3("getCellIndicesFlat", "AffymetrixCdfFile", function(this,
..., force=FALSE) {
chipType <- getChipType(this);

# Look for results in file cache
key <- list(method="getCellIndicesFlat", class=class(this)[1],
chipType=chipType);
dirs <- c("aroma.affymetrix", chipType);
if (!.force) {
map <- loadCache(key=key, dirs=dirs);
if (!is.null(map))
return(map);
}

# Calculate results
cells <- getCellIndices(this);
map <- flattenCellIndices(cells);

# Save to cache
saveCache(indices, key=key, dirs=dirs);

map;
})

Cache computational expensive results to file is something we do quite
a bit in aroma.affymetrix, especially for CDF data.
